answer.conclusion: Ferret's self-dogfooding is an oracle discipline, not a demo: `scripts/dogfood.mjs` (15 checks, +3 with `--content`) asks Ferret about Ferret **over MCP only**, and every answer is computed independently from `git` or from arithmetic in the script; `scripts/dogfood-db.mjs` maintains the persistent `ferret-dogfood` Postgres container that `.mcp.json` points at. A new session needs three things it cannot read out of the tree: the per-machine `.local/ferret-config` grant (the oracle needs `config.read` on top of `read,record,mutate,index`, and no doc's remediation string says so), the fact that `exclude` is read-path-only because EPIC-135 is PROPOSED and deliberately unimplemented, and the uncommitted in-flight real-agent benchmark plus the `src/config/exclusions.ts` trailing-slash fix it found. Without those it will re-report deliberate exclusions as missing-file defects, assume excluded content is not stored, and repeat claims that have already been reversed (raw-`ts_rank` scores, durable context being unsearchable, `ferret_find` having no offset).
key_facts: The harness is two scripts: `scripts/dogfood.mjs` (`npm run dogfood`, `-- --check`, `-- --content`) and `scripts/dogfood-db.mjs` (`npm run dogfood:db`, `--index` after a merge, `--no-content`, `--stop`). Owning Epics: EPIC-118 (IMPLEMENTED) and EPIC-134 (IMPLEMENTED/VALIDATED).

Two invariants define the discipline: every question has an answer produced independently of Ferret, and every question goes through the MCP surface rather than SQL — "a defect that only SQL can see is not a defect a client will ever hit" (scripts/dogfood.mjs:5-17).

Configuration is per-machine and untracked: `.mcp.json` sets `FERRET_CONFIG_HOME` to `.local/ferret-config`, and `.local/` is gitignored. A fresh checkout therefore has no exclusions and no permission grant, so re-indexing pulls the benchmark answer keys into the store.

The grant matters and both records under-state it. `dogfood.mjs:449` and `:470` and the EPIC-134 validation reproduce block name only `["read","record","mutate"]` / `+"index"`; the exclusion check calls `ferret_config_exclusions`, which needs `config.read` (src/authorization/authorization.ts:46). Without it `exclusionFor` returns undefined and every excluded-but-tracked path is reported as a missing file — the defect #211 (d51f122) fixed. `LOCAL_OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL` defaults to index/read/record only (authorization.ts:204).

EPIC-135 (Exclusion Enforcement at Ingestion) is **PROPOSED, awaiting owner approval, deliberately not implemented** by owner decision 2026-09-07. `exclude` is enforced on the read path only: on the dogfood store, 27 `file` and 43 `file_version` entities existed for excluded paths with 1,463,485 bytes of content retained, created while the exclusion was in force. Reads (`ferret_find`, `ferret_search`, `ferret_context_pack`) do exclude them.

EPIC-135 §14 deliberately inverts the dogfood rule: its acceptance criteria must be evaluated against storage, not the MCP surface, because the defect is defined by what is retained. Both rules stand and answer different questions.

answer.conclusion: A session's memories are private to the agent that ran it — `ferret_session_recall`/`_show` refuse any session whose `actorId` isn't the calling principal, and `_list` has no actor field at all (EPIC-133). The decision becomes readable by a different agent only once it reaches the durable tier: the owning agent calls `ferret_context_promote` (owner-only, `actorId` from the composition root) or records it directly with `ferret_context_record`. From there any agent reads it via `ferret_context_find`, `ferret_context_trust`, `ferret_context_pack` (durable context first), or `ferret_search` restricted to `kinds: ['context']`. One extra hop applies to extracted memories: they promote as `candidate`, which `ferret_context_find` excludes until an agent holding `MUTATE` accepts them via `ferret_context_lifecycle`.

answer.conclusion: A session's memories stay private to the agent that ran the session: `ferret_session_recall` and `ferret_session_show` refuse any session the calling principal does not own, and `ferret_session_list` only lists that principal's own sessions. The one route across the boundary is `ferret_context_promote`, which the session's own owner must call; promoted statements then live in the shared durable tier that any agent with READ can query. Memories recorded explicitly become current context immediately, whereas extraction-derived ones land as candidates and need `ferret_context_lifecycle` accept before a default `ferret_context_find` shows them.

`ferret_session_list` takes no actor parameter and lists only `sessions.sessionsFor(principal.id, ...)` (src/mcp/session-tools.ts:310-318).

`ferret_context_promote` refuses unless `session.actorId === actorId`, with `actorId` supplied by the composition root (`principal.id`), never by tool input (src/mcp/context-tools.ts:288-308; src/mcp/server.ts:334).
Promotion only ever considers memories, never captures/transcripts, and refuses superseded ones (src/context/promotion.ts:11-32, 80-82).

An EXPLICIT memory (recorded via `ferret_session_remember`) promotes to `LifecycleState.ACTIVE`; an extracted one promotes to `CANDIDATE` (src/context/promotion.ts:92-93), and `ferret_context_find` excludes proposed/superseded/archived statements unless asked for by name (src/mcp/context-tools.ts:327-336) — so a candidate needs `ferret_context_lifecycle` accept to be seen by default.

Durable context itself is agent-independent and shared: EPIC-132 AC-1/AC-2/AC-10 assert one agent reads what another recorded, sees who stated it, and that neither agent holds a store of its own (docs/EPICs/EPIC-132-Multi-Agent-Shared-Context.md:74-83).

Security tests drive this against real MCP clients and PostgreSQL: 'refuses to read another agent’s session', identical refusal for an unknown id, and 'refuses to publish another agent’s session as shared context' (tests/security/context-governance.test.ts:167-205).
